name: Electric Bicycle
description: Alaska's statutes have no electric bicycle category, so on public roads one is a motor-driven cycle. The term is defined only for state parks: a bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes, the first under 500 watts.

restrictions.rule: In state parks, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph with a motor under 500 watts, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph (11 AAC 12.990(15))
On public roads it isn't a bicycle, which Alaska defines as propelled only by human power, but a motor-driven cycle: the rider needs a driver's license, or at 14 or 15 an M2 permit
In state parks, any class may ride roads open to cars or motorcycles and trails open to off-road vehicles (11 AAC 12.115)

In state parks, only Class 1 may ride trails open to bicycles, including campground, picnic-area and paved trails, unless a trail is posted closed; a fat-tire Class 1 may ride wherever fat-tire bicycles may (11 AAC 12.115)
A state park director may temporarily close a trail or area to e-bikes to protect the land, reduce user conflicts or for safety (11 AAC 12.115)
